# Datasets
```{r}
offence <-read.csv("cleaned_offence_breakdown_complete.csv")
ta <- read.csv("cleaned_merged_rates.csv")
head(offence)

```
# Data Preparation
```{r}
#result <- csv_data[csv_data$salary > 60000, c("name", "salary")]
theft <- offence[offence$ANZSOC.Division =='Theft',c("Territorial.Authority","FY_Year","ANZSOC.Division", "Victimisations")]
head(theft)

```
```{r}

head(ta)
population <- ta[,c("Territorial.Authority","Year","Population")]
head (population)
```
```{r}
library(dplyr) 
theft <- rename(theft, c("Year"="FY_Year"))
```

```{r}
head(theft)
```


```{r}
library("dplyr")                                               
library("plyr")                                            
library("readr")
mdata <- merge(theft, population, by= c("Territorial.Authority","Year"))
```

```{r}
head(mdata)
sum(is.na(mdata))
dim(mdata)
```


```{r}
mdata$Theft_rate <- (mdata$Victimisations/mdata$Population * 1000)
mdata$log_population <- (log(mdata$Population))
```

```{r}
head(mdata)
```


```{r}
mdata$log_population <- (log(mdata$Population))
```

# Correlation Stage

```{r}
plot(x = mdata$Population, y = mdata$Theft_rate,
    xlab = "Population",

    main = "Population vs Theft_rate"
)


```
### Log Transformation of Population Applied
```{r}
plot(x = mdata$log_population, y = mdata$Theft_rate,
```

## Spearman & Pearson Correlation
```{r}
library(psych)
mdata%>%
dplyr::select(log_population, Theft_rate)%>% pairs.panels(method = "spearman", hist.col = "lightgreen", density = TRUE, ellipses = FALSE )
```
```{r}
mdata%>%
dplyr::select(log_population, Theft_rate)%>% pairs.panels(method = "pearson", hist.col = "lightgreen", density = TRUE, ellipses = FALSE )
```


```{r}
cor.test(mdata$log_population, mdata$Theft_rate, alternative = "two.sided", method = "pearson", conf.level = 0.95)
```
```{r}
cor.test(mdata$log_population, mdata$Theft_rate, alternative = "two.sided", method = "spearman")
```
 
### *Spearman will be used and focused on as main result because theft rate is right-skewed and the spread widens on the right.*

## Correlation & Results Table

```{r}
library(pander)
test_type <- c("Pooled Pearson", "Pooled Spearman", "Spearman FY2023", "Spearman FY2024", "Spearman FY2025")
n_val <- c(201, 201, 67,67,67)
coef_val  <- c(0.616, 0.626, 0.653,0.603, 0.629)
ci_val    <- c("[0.52, 0.70]", "-", "-", "-", "-") 
p_val     <- c("<0.001", "<0.001", "<0.001", "<0.001", "<0.001")

corr_table <- data.frame(test_type, n_val, coef_val, ci_val, p_val)
names(corr_table) <- c("Correlation Type", "n", "Coefficient", "95% CI", "p-value")
pander(corr_table, round = 3, align = 'c')

```


## K-fold Validation


```{r}
set.seed(0)                       # any number, so your folds can be repeated
k <- 10                            # number of folds (check your notes)

# Step 1: one fold number per TA, not per row
tas <- unique(mdata$Territorial.Authority)
fold_of_ta <- sample(rep(1:k, length.out = length(tas)))              # random fold number for each TA
names(fold_of_ta) <- tas # join the fold number back onto mdata, so a TA's 3 rows share it
mdata$fold <- unname(fold_of_ta[mdata$Territorial.Authority])

```



```{r}
set.seed(256)                       
k <- 10                           


tas <- unique(mdata$Territorial.Authority)
fold_of_ta <- sample(rep(1:k, length.out = length(tas)))            
names(fold_of_ta) <- tas 
mdata$fold <- unname(fold_of_ta[mdata$Territorial.Authority])


rmse <- numeric(k)
for (i in 1:k) {
  train <- mdata[mdata$fold != i, ]                    
  test  <- mdata[mdata$fold == i, ]                     

  fit  <- lm(log(Theft_rate) ~ log_population, data = train)
  pred <- exp(predict(fit, newdata = test))     

         
  rmse[i] <- sqrt(mean((test$Theft_rate - pred)^2))
}


mean(rmse)                          
```


```{r}
summary(model2)
confint(model2)
```

```{r}
sd(mdata$Theft_rate)                        
```
```{r}
rmse_base <- numeric(k)
for (i in 1:k) {
  train <- mdata[mdata$fold != i, ]
  test  <- mdata[mdata$fold == i, ] 

  pred <- rep(mean(train$Theft_rate), nrow(test))    

  rmse_base[i] <- sqrt(mean((test$Theft_rate - pred)^2))
}
mean(rmse_base)
```
```{r}
mean(rmse)
mean(rmse_base)
```
```{r}
range(rmse)
range(rmse_base)
```

```{r}
plot(x = 1:k, y = rmse, type = "b", col = "blue", lwd = 3,
    xlab = "Fold Number",
    ylab = "Cross-Validation RMSE",
    main = "K-fold Cross-Validation RMSE",
    ylim = c(6, 28))

lines(x = 1:k, y = rmse_base, col = "red", lwd = 3, lty= 2, type = "b")

legend(x = "topleft", lty = c(1,2), text.font = 2, lwd = 2.5,
       col= c("blue","red"),text.col = c("blue", "red"), 
       legend=c("K-fold RMSE", "Baseline RMSE"))
```
```{r}
library(pander)

model_rmse <- c(12.564)
base_rmse  <- c(15.396)
difference <- c(2.832)    
sd_value   <- c(15.880)

rmse_table <- data.frame(model_rmse, base_rmse, difference, sd_value)
names(rmse_table) <- c("Model RMSE", "Baseline RMSE", "Difference", "Standard Deviation")
pander(rmse_table, round = 2, align = 'c')

```
